disease_label_per_paper: Relapsing polychondritis initiating with fever of unknown origin and bilateral auricular perichondritis
presentation_summary: 58-year-old woman referred with 1 month of spiking fever above 38.5 C and fever of unknown origin after no response to antibiotics.
On admission she reported chills and nonproductive cough; otologic examination showed tender swollen red pinnae with characteristic lobule sparing.
The paper reported no nasal, ocular, tracheal cartilage tenderness, tracheal stenosis on chest CT, aortic root dilation, or aortic regurgitation at that time.
Admission labs showed anemia, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, ESR 72 mm/hr, CRP 11.64 mg/dL, ferritin 548 ng/mL, negative ANA/ANCA/anti-CCP, negative blood culture, and negative CMV antigenemia.
Pinna biopsy showed perichondritis with inflammatory infiltrates and cartilage destruction; fever and auricular swelling resolved with prednisolone followed by methotrexate steroid-sparing therapy.

risk_context.source_text_value: she had not responded to antibiotic therapy

observations.source_text_value: high fever of up to 38.4 C on admission; history of spiking fever >38.5 C
spiking fever (>38.5 C) of 1-month duration; FUO
tender and swollen pinnae with obvious redness of both ears
There was no abnormality of the nose
There was no abnormality of the eyes
chest CT showed neither interstitial pneumonia nor tracheal stenosis
Neither aortic root dilatation nor aortic regurgitation was observed by echocardiography

confirmatory_findings.finding: Pinna biopsy showed auricular perichondritis and cartilage destruction
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: cellular infiltrates of lymphocytes, neutrophils, and plasma cells at the cartilage-skin interface with reduced chondrocytes in areas of cartilage destruction

confirmatory_findings.finding: Final diagnosis of relapsing polychondritis by McAdam-Damiani-Levine criteria
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: fulfilled the McAdam-Damiani-Levine criteria for the diagnosis of RP

confirmatory_findings.finding: Steroid response with resolution of fever and auricular swelling
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: prednisolone daily led to improvement; fever and auricular swelling disappeared

actual_treatment: methotrexate 6 mg weekly then 8 mg weekly during taper
actual_outcome: Three months after discharge prednisolone was reduced to 12.5 mg daily and no subsequent RP flare-up was reported.
